CT Terminology (August 30, 2006)
AAPM
Association for the Advancement of Physicists in Medicine
ACR
American College of Radioligists
AGP
Accelerated Graphics Port is an interface specification that enables 3-D graphics to display quickly on 
personal computers
Anet 
Offline workstation for the Tshiba A-series scanner not sold as an option here but many of the functions 
are included in the display console
APMC / PMC
Patient Motion Correction algorith that corrects for artifacts caused by patient movement during a scan
BIR
Bio Imaging Research - company that makes image the reconstruction boards and software
BMC
Beam Motion correction Not used on 4 and 16 Multi slice systems
BMD:
Beam Motion Detector is two solid state detectors which measure the change of X-ray tube focus 
position comparing the change in x-ray dose as the anode shifts due to heat.(Not Used)
BMS
Bone Mineral Study Not used on Toshiba CT scanners in USA
Bridge PWB:
The Bridge Printed Circuit Board connects one cPCI chassis to another cPCI Chassis. In the 
Reconstruction processor the bridge is a slave to the RTM and master of the second chassis.(not used on 
CBTB
CD-R 
Compact Disk Recordable media
CI
Continuous imaging includes CT flouro, Real time helical and sure start. Collimator:
The collimator is mounted at the bottom of the X-ray tube to shape and remove the excess x-rays. CP5:
Circuit protector 5. Vertical drive motor circuit breaker in couch(over current relay ). CP51:
Circuit protector 51. Horizontal drive motor circuit breaker in couch (over current relay). cPCI Chassis:
compact Peripheral Component Interconnect chassis This is a connection enclosure for the MHR boards 
in the reconstructioin unit
CPU 
Central Processing Unit the central unit in a computer containing the logic circuitry that performs the 
instructions of a computer's programs
CT Port:
Is an option that comprises extra localizing lasers and software for therapy planning.(not used on super4 
Yet)

How to Install and Use Jaws Editor 

What is Jaws PDF Editor? Jaws editor enables you to view, edit and save PDF files on 
computers running on Windows NT, Windows 2000, and Windows XP without running a 
full version of Adobe Acrobat. Jaws allows you to navigate through pdf documents via 
bookmarks, the page list, thumbnails, or links. You can also extract pages from a pdf file 
or rotate pages when necessary. Jaws Editor enables you to add your own notes and highlighting to the pdf reference 
documents and manuals that you carry with you to the site on your laptop. Installing Jaws PDF Editor on your laptop 
 
Open the Class CD

3. Right click anywhere on your desktop to open a new folder 
4. Name the folder “_______ Class CD”. Copy the contents of your CD to the new folder. In Windows Explorer → My Computer, click on the CD ROM drive (probably your D:\

the screen

•
2nd error: request for view replacement

One view replacement is tolerated - no significant image quality loss
Two or more view replacements in a single scan causes image quality loss - error 
is displayed

“broadcasting”

 Toshiba America Medical Systems, Inc. Configure CT to Send “ ^ “ as the Delimiter between Name Components 
 
Complaint(s): 
A space is used as the delimiter between name components in DICOM tag (0010,0010). As the result, 
the entire patient name appears in the last name field of Storage SCP devices. DICOM v3.0 specifies to 
use “ ^ “ as the delimiter between name components. Version(s): 
All versions of CT A-series scanners 
 
Resolution(s): 
By enabling this function, only the patient name, DICOM tag (0010,0010), will be send with “ ^ “ 
between each of 5 name components as shown below … 
 
[last name]^[first name]^[middle name]^[prefix]^[suffix] 
 
Example: 
SMITH^JOHN^J^MR^MD 
BROWN^MARY^M^MS^MD

Purpose: In order to ensure that the Toshiba CT scanner at your institution will 
encounter minimal or no image quality problems during the ACR testing process, this 
document is designed to help you complete a run-through of the testing process. This 
guide is intended to be a supplement to the “Instruction Manual For Testing the ACR CT 
Phantom” put out by the ACR. Materials: You will need an ACR phantom. Other phantoms cannot be substituted for 
the run-through. Please note the phantom is labeled with “Head,” “Foot,” “Top,” and 
“Bottom” for orientation. The phantom is described in full on page 2 of the ACR 
instructions. A copy of the “Instruction Manual for Testing the ACR CT Phantom” should be kept on 
hand for reference and more detailed explanations of the specific tests involved. A copy of the “CT Phantom Site Scanning Data Form” should be used to record the 
protocol and test results (as the customer will during the actual test). Tests: The following tests should be performed: 
 
• Positioning Accuracy 
• CT Number Accuracy 
• Slice Width 
• Low Contrast Resolution 
• High Contrast Resolution 
• CT Number Uniformity 
• Image noise 
 
Important Note About Tests: Please pay particular attention to the CT Number 
Accuracy Test and the Low Contrast Resolution Test. Important Note About Protocols: Each test will be performed using either a chest or 
abdomen protocol. These protocols must be the ones used by the site. Do NOT use the 
example protocol given by the ACR or the standard Toshiba protocol. The only 
exceptions are 1) if the site actually uses the standard Toshiba protocol or 2) if the site

Toshiba protocol may be substituted. Otherwise, unless specifically instructed, the only adjustment to the site’s protocol that is

1. Outline 
This document describes the procedures for adjusting VR3 which has been added to 
the new XC PWB PX71-07030 Gr. 2 for Aquilion-series systems. With this adjustment, the waveform at the tube voltage leading edge is optimally 
adjusted, which can reduce X-ray tube loading. Design change applicable systems and serial numbers: Aquilion systems with serial 
numbers 2148 and later and the system installed in Osaka Hoshigaoka Hospital 

- 2 -

(1) This work must be performed in the following cases. <1> XC PWB replacement (PX71-07030 Gr. 2) 
<2> SRU-H replacement (when PX71-07030 Gr. 2 is used as the XC PWB) 
Adjustment is usually not required for tube replacement. Adjustment should be 
performed, however, if the check finds a shift in the waveform. (2) Do not touch any VRs other than VR3. Doing so may adversely affect the kV or 
mA precision. Instruments, tools, and time required

capacitance. The high resistance (megaohms) of the Bleeder will make the

XC error trouble shooting 

Principle components 
 
The X-ray system comprises the X-ray tube, and a High voltage generator (power 
supply), a CPU and a stator controller. When the system detects an X-ray control error it will give an XC error on the console. Good work practice notes. Read the x-ray service manual. Read CT-FSM-1174 
Perform routine maintenance procedures as specified by the Preventative maintenance 
manual. Especially the IF adjustment procedure. Make sure you have backed up the IF data from the XC log in the last 3 months. The file 
labeling should be seg#tube#date.ifd I recommend that you create a folder on your laptop 
for each site and save such information for each site in the folder. This can be used for 
restoring the IF data to the XC pwb in the case that a new board is installed without any 
data or in the case that you want to reload know good data. You can also FTP site-specific information to the service directory on the scanner for 
other CE s use. Be very careful in ordering replacement parts that you specify the same revision and 
group no for the part. The Aquilion X-ray generator has gone thru various revisions and 
many parts are not compatible. If the same part is not available check CT-FSM-???,CT-FSM-? And CT-FSM-? for 
compatibility 
 
When you download the XC logs use the following file labeling format. Seg#tube#date.log 
This will allow minimize confusion if you send your log file to NTS for their help in 
diagnosing problems. Before doing any exposures download the error log and check for fault conditions. If the fault is with the x-ray tube starter you can damage the tube by performing multiple 
exposures without the tube anode rotating. Note: The detection circuit for detecting anode rotation failure is not very reliable. If you 
are not sure check the rotor by sound or touch. Always check the rotor is working after

Applications logs
the system monitors anything that is programmed as an “event” 
and stores the results in the Applications log
We can identify what events were recorded when the system failed 
by:
knowing what the system time was during the event
searching for key words
We can evaluate the events that took place prior to the fault for 
additional causes. Applications Logs
The current Applications Event log is the applications event log that the 
system is currently using. Anytime the system is re-booted the current applications event log is 
closed, zipped and stored in the G partition of the system disk drive 
under the eventlog directory. The file labeling structure for the zipped Applications Event Logs are as 
follows:
errlog.ApplEvent.YYYYMMMDD-HHMMSS.Evt.gz

Applications Logs
As an example for April 27 2006 at 02:38:29
errlog.ApplEvent.2006Apr27-023829.Evt.gz
This date stamp of April 27 at 02:38:29 represents the time of when the 
event log was saved and will start with the previous shutdown process, 
the system power-up and all of time in between. These logs can be unzipped and viewed by the windows event viewer 
program
They can be converted from an evt file to a txt file for viewing buy more 
applications
When saving as text the data needs to be sorted oldest first for easy 
reading. Applications Logs
When converting from a event file to a text file on your PC, here 
are some things to be careful of:
Your PC is set to the same time zone as the CT that you are 
converting the log files from. Because your PC does not have the same registry information and 
DLL files as the CT system, the following error can happen:
Register information missing
Register descriptions are not correct, sometimes shifted
Error codes missing

summary:
“TaskStarter error” 
 
Outline 
This is a guide to troubleshooting a taskstarter error on the Aquilion series with the MHR 
reconstruction boards 
 
Systems 
Super 4, Aquilion16 or Aquilion64 
 
The Problem: 
After power on, the scan side application fails to boot. The message “TaskStarter Start-up failed” 
is displayed on the scan side and the display side boots normally. When information is selected on the dialog box, the message “Cannot connect to RTM” is 
displayed. The cause 
As part of the boot up sequence, the scan side workstation connects to the RTM board via the fiber 
channel. It will then download the configuration to the RTM board. If the system cannot connect to the RTM during the boot up sequence, it will display this message 
and the boot process will halt. The method 
1. Confirm that VxWorks is not loading on the RTM board. Connect your laptop to the RTM 
board using HyperTerminal or Terra Term. Use a connection setup of 9600, n, 8, and 1. Boot 
the scanner and see if the OS (VxWorks) loads on the RTM board. You should see the 
VxWorks graphic displayed. On the Aquilion64 slice system check both rack 1 and rack 2 
RTM boards. If VxWorks does not get displayed, a power supply may be faulty, a board on 
the PCI bus may be hanging up the RTM, or the RTM board may be faulty. Check the power supplies in the REC box. (24V, 3.3V) 

Note: On an Aquilion64/32 the RTM boards can be swapped from the top rack to the bottom rack 
to check if it is the RTM board or the rack and associated power supplies. It may be easier to start 
with this before removing all the MHR boards or the PCI chassis bridge. If you determine the 
RTM board is faulty go to (4) 
 
3. Check the LED’s on the MHR boards and the RTM board. If one MHR has no lights on, 
remove this board from the PCI chassis and reboot the scanner. If this board was hanging the 
bus, VxWorks will be displayed and the system will boot to the application. Order the faulty 
MHR board. If the LED’s appear similar  ...

Commercial Option Licences
Commercial option licences are generally supplied on floppy disk (licence floppy). A new licence
floppy can be used on any compatible CT system, however it should be used only on the CT

console onto which the licence is loaded. The licence can be unloaded from the CT system
console onto the linked licence floppy, by which the licence floppy is renewed. Commercial options may comprise additional hardware and may require dedicated application
training for the operators. Option licences should therefore be handled with care. Commercial option licences should not be confused with CT system component licences such

disk should be identified and only that disk should be replaced. The procedure

source: CT_64slice_docs__6_Problems with solutions__5_Aquilion16__Aquilion16 F&S - Operating system not found.pdf
summary:
Updated 25 December 2006 
Aquilion S16 Failure and Solutions – Broken System disk 

Summary 
 
Console (Scan or Display) will not boot and message “Operating System not 
found” is displayed. Solution: make sure that the boot order in BIOS is set correctly. Phenomenon 
 
When starting up the system the message "Operating system not found" is 
displayed. Explanation 
 
It appears that there is a problem with the operating system or with the system 
disk itself. Solution 
 
Check the BIOS settings for the Boot sequence. Under normal circumstances 
the Boot sequence in the BIOS should look like the picture below. Operating System not found 

In case of a system disk failure an error is detected in the DOS environment 
saying “Boot-disk failure”. When this happens the BIOS setting is automatically 
changed such that the image disk is put first, and remains this way even after a 
new system disk is inserted. It looks as follows: 

Automatically the BIOS sets the SCSI image-disk on top of the boot-sequence. If 
software is loaded at this stage, it will load onto the image-disk rather than the 
system-disk. When you select the correct Boot-sequence again, in order to load 
software on the system-disk, disk partitioning is already performed on the image 
disk and Disk-management window is a big mess. The only way to correct this is 
to go into Disk-management and delete the partitions and virtual disks, created 
by previous software loading attempt. After this create, rename and format new 
E: and H: partitions with the Disk-management and reload software from scratch. After that the disk should look like shown below. In this case the main cause is the automatic changes in the BIOS setting. If BIOS setting is still correct then the system disk should be replaced.

source: CT_64slice_docs__6_Problems with solutions__5_Aquilion16__Aquilion16 F&S - Scan cannot be performed.pdf
summary:
10 October 2006 
Aquilion16 Failure and solution - Scan cannot be performed 

Contents 
 
1. Phenomenon 
2. Procedure 
3. Solution 

1. Phenomenon 
 
Upon starting a scan the gantry spins up, the abort button lights for a moment, then the 
light extinguishes. The Start button does not light. The Exam-plan window does not 
close and the gantry keeps spinning. There is no access to windows using the shortcuts. It is not possible to type the 
password for engineer utility. It is not possible to access the System Setup menu via ctrl-
alt-t. "System reset" (mouse in upper left corner) does not seem to work. Shutdown does 
not seem to work, although it shuts down the D-console. The system was switched off, even though S-console was not properly shut down. Upon 
reboot recovery process runs for the S-console. Procedure 
 
From the D-console access to the S-console via telnet (kingbird user) is available, which 
means that the CPU (PC) is running and operating system is working. Started "hwtest" in a telnet session from the D console. The program does not start (the 
menu is not displayed and the window hangs up.) The telnet session had to be ended 
using the Windows task-manager on the D-console. Boot-up of the scan console is slow. The D console shows a yellow message that it 
cannot connect to the S-console and asks whether to wait or continue. The Aquilion logo 
is shown after clicking continue. Icons for gantry/couch and OLP are being displayed on the S-console only after an 
unusually long time. The Aquilion logo is not displayed on the S-console. MHR diagnostics was tried and showed a problem with the MHR-BP board in slot 12. This result was reproduced during a second run of the test. Solution 
 
Replaced the MHR-BP board in slot 12.

updated 31 May 2006

Summary

Summary 
 
On an Aquilion32/64 a band ring artefact appeared. This problem was caused by the detector and eventually cured by replacement of the 
detector assembly. Phenomenon 
 
A band ring artefact as per figure 1 shows in helical 32x1mm L-Field. Figure 1 
Band ring artefact

Analysis by DCA shows that channels 681 - 704 have bad data. See figure 2 and 3. Figure 2 
Bad data on channel 681 and up 

Figure 3 
Bad data up to and including channel 704 
2/3 

All 24 bad channels (681 through 704) are processed by the QV2 board in slot 30. The channels are also processed by ADC2 board in slot 15, but that board also 
processes channels 657 through 680. The QV2 board in slot 30 is therefore suspected 
most. Air calibrations were attempted but did not help. It should be noted that it is unlikely that 
calibrations can compensate for artefacts of this nature. Swopping boards in combination with further calibrations caused some confusion: 
- 
QV2 in slot 30 swapped with QV2 in slot 38 and the artefact was gone; 
- 
Swapped back QV2 boards to original locations - artefact did not show; 
- 
Carried out air calibration - artefact returned! - 
Replaced QV2 slot 30 with a new QV2 - no artefact; 
- 
Carried out NRA calibration - artefact returned! - 
ADC2 in slot 15 swapped with ADC2 in slot 19 - initially no artefact but after 
about 30 minutes artefact re-appeared. If the power to R-base is switched off for 
about 10sec - no artefact for a certain time. Even though confusing this exercise shows that no matter which boards are swopped or 
replaced, the problem persists. Aquilion32/64 systems do not bundle the channels on the backplane. The detector has 
38 block with 24 channels each. The 38 QV2 boards match the detector blocks, with the 
exception that the first 16 channels of the first block are not used, hence also th ...

summary:
Updated, 21 March 2007 
Aquilion64 Solution - Cannot mount MOD for image/raw data 

Problem 
After loading Application software V3.00 on an Aquilion64, the MOD could not be 
mounted anymore from the Image Data Utility, and neither from the Raw Data Utility. This Aquilion64 was equipped with the optional MOD drive (CMO-12A) in addition to 
the standard DVD/Multi drive. Checks and Solution 
Check that the drive letter of the MOD (Removable Disk) is set to P, using Windows 
Explorer. If it is not P, then select "CT System Shutdown" from the Windows Start menu on the 
Display console. Wait until the Logon window is displayed. Logon as Administrator (toshibact) 
Select: Start - Run and execute the following command: 
 
C:\install\ChangeDriveletter.exe -c -r 
 
This will automatically reboot the computer. (Alternatively, use Windows Disk Management to reassign letter P to the MOD drive.) 

If the problem persists, execute the following procedures to set up MOD again: 
 
Open a Korn Shell and point to X: 
 
cd /toshiba/bin/ 
./set_isac_inf.exe 
---------------------------------------------------------------- 
 MW MOD SCSI Inf. output (x:/toshiba/system_data/dev/isac0) 
 ctrl = 1, id = 5, drive = [P] 
 ---------------------------------------------------------------- 
cd / 
exit 
 
Reboot the system.

summary:
Finding a broken laser diode assy on Aquilion32/64 
 
Laser diode mount assy 
PX79-12945 Gr1. In stationary mode all Rotational channels send out data. The data is checked only by RS1 and RS0. When turning gantry clockwise by hand (front side Gantry) 
with motor control switched off (black button) 
At a certain point where one of the laser diodes is broken 
The following led indication was shown first RS1 then RS0 
on the GCIFV1 board. RS1 fail 

 RS0 fail 
 
Don't forget to clear the error when the laser moves from RS1 to RS0 (this is the order in which the problem 
should occur when you turn the gantry clockwise) and place a mark on the rotating part when the error is 
visible, so you know the location of the corresponding LD-assy. Remove the MUDAT section which holds CH1 and CH0 in order to get access to the laser diodes, and 
replace broken LD assy. Before changing the laser diode assy please read FSM-CT3368

Aquilion64 - Examplan tab shows 1111 after upgrade to V3.1 
 
System

Problem 
After upgrading the software from V2.04 ER004 to V3.10 ER004 the exam plan preset 
screen showed an abnormality. When selecting this tab, part of the screen becomes blank and the systems seems to 
hang up. olution 
under Customize in the Exam Plan Utility 
 
S
Select Init

A-series Technical Service Training 
Practical Exercises 
Problem: 
 
On an Aquilion64, one or more of the following messages on the console monitor: 
 
- error in preprocessing 
- no message 
- gantry disconnected during scan 

Procedure 
 
Check the errlog.BIR file for tISPDc and GCIFA-D 

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ 
** ** 
** Log for Rack #1 ** 
** (See below for Rack #2) ** 
** ** 
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ 
 
Errors Found 
------------ 
E11> RTM Problem occurred in task tPRE 
 errno:0, 0xc0010014: CMD_PRE_GANTRY_ERROR from GIF 
E12> RTM Problem occurred in task tPRE 
 PRE reported error status for a scan: 0xc0010014 
 
GCIFA-D Information: 
 -File-------Flash Version: 03.01.1325 
 ---HW-------Flash Version: 03.01.1325 
 -File-Application Version: 03.02.1381

TARGET.c 385 tISPDc4 | GCIFA-D Error: 0x3

DC rail voltage is monitored in SRU-H (filter-H pwb) and sent to XC pwb via cable S74B and connector CNN74B. If voltage is OK on the DC rail (270 - 320 VDC), but in [Status info] the [Detected AC] is showing 0 V, one of the following parts is likely to be defective:

- signal cable S74B

summary:
25 December 2006 
Aquilion32/64 Failure & Solution - No 280V DC from Spellman AC 

Phenomenon 
 
No 280V DC from the AC Unit, while 200V AV input is ok. Solution 
 
Replacement of the AC unit did not solve the problem. Replacement of the HV Multiplier 
Unit did solve the problem. Background 
 
The control of the thyristors in the AC Unit is done by the AC/Filament Feedback board 
in the HV Multiplier Unit. That circuit board cannot be replaced individually hence 
replacement of the HV Multiplier Unit was necessary.

Updated 25 December 2006 
Aquilion32/64 Failure & Solution - Spellman 72kW Generator 

Summary 
 
On the Aquilion32/64, used for training at the METC, in the evening of the second day 
of use, an XC error was observed. The problem was solved by replacing all Spellman boxes, however the Inverter unit was 
the actual defective part. Phenomenon 
 
Upon starting a scan an XC error was displayed and a burning smell could be observed 
in the scan room. The error was 100% reproducible. Indications 
 
The error details were: Under mA (Fixed), Under kV (Fixed) and Abnormal HFG. The errors could be reproduced easily, also by performing X-ray tube warm-up. The burning smell seemed to originate from the inverter unit, for which a malfunction 
inside the inverter unit was thought to be the most likely cause of the problem. Alternatively the tube was suspected. Replacement of all Spellman boxes solved the problem though. Investigation at the Spellman factory revealed that the inverter unit had developed an 
internal short between a circuit board and a capacitor. Solution 
 
Replacement of the entire Spellman generator. In this case replacement of the inverter 
unit only would most likely have been sufficient.

source: CT_64slice_docs__6_Problems with solutions__7_Aquilion3264__Muhlenberg MPR Streak Artifact Evaluation.pdf
summary:
Muhlenberg Community Hospital
MPR Streak Artifact Evaluation 
Thursday, November 20, 2008 | Mike Lacey National Support Specialist CT

Image Quality Complaint
Excessive streak artifacts in 
the sagittal and coronal MPR 
images at the base of the brain. Currently there is no reported 
image quality issue with the 
axial images that were used to 
build these sagittal and coronal 
images. This same artifact in 
the sagittal and coronal MPR 
images was present on all five 
clinical studies that were sent 
in for evaluation. Source of the artifact:
The root cause of this image quality issue is from a Windmill 
Artifact in the source axial images used to build the MPR 
image files. A Windmill artifact is caused by not satisfying the Nyquist 
criteria in the Z axis of the patient, or more simply put the table 
speed was too fast for the slice width and scanning parameters 
currently being used and the data points could not be correctly 
interpolated affecting the Z axis image quality. Source of the artifact:
This type of an artifact can be 
easily seen when all of the 
source axial images are stepped 
through and viewed at once 
with the Image Selector. There 
is a swirl pattern rotating 
clockwise from any bone points 
in the anatomy that moves in 
the z axis through the image 
files. It looks like the point of 
a windmill turning as you step 
through the image files. Source of the artifact:
This artifact is also easily 
seen in the neck of this glass 
gar filled with water. How to correct this artifact:
Change the acquisition slice width from the current setting of 
1.0 mm by 16 with a HP 11 to an acquisition slice width of 0.5 
mm by 16 with a HP11. This will double the sampling time 
and eliminate the artifact.

Mike Lacey

Event Logs
• Application Logs
– Applications Error Records
• Security Logs
– Security Audit Records
• System Logs
– System Error Records

Applications logs
• Monitors the system for anything that is programmed as 
an “event” and stores the results in the Applications log
• By searching for key words we can identify what events 
were recorded when the system failed. • By knowing what the system time was during the event 
will also help in isolating a system failure. • Can evaluate what took place prior to the fault 
happening for additional causes. Applications Logs
• The current Applications Event log is defined as the 
applications event log that the system is currently using. • Anytime the system is re-booted the current applications 
event log is closed, zipped and stored in the G partition 
of the system disk drive under the eventlog directory. • The file structure for the zipped Applications Event Logs 
are as follows:
– errlog.ApplEvent.YYYYMMMDD-HHMMSS.Evt.gz

Recommended Modality Worklist Configuration (COT-32) 
Introduction  
Modality Worklist (COT-32) option allows CT to query RIS directly or via RIS Broker for a list of matching scheduled work 
orders and retrieve them back into CT so that technologists can simply select an order from the worklist window for 
scanning rather than manually register each patient, which easily making typographical errors and slow down the entire 
CT workflow. Note that CT only specifies the matching key criteria but it is RIS that does the actual search and filtering of the work 
order database. CT must accept and display everything RIS sends. Applicable Model(s) & Version(s)

Multislice HELICAL CT SCANNER
APPLICATION
The Aquilion is a multislice Helical CT system that supports
whole-body scanning. The system generates 64 slices per second using the
Selectable Slice-thickness Multi-row Detector (SSMD). In addition, the high-speed rotation mechanism and the
fast reconstruction unit of the system allow quick image
acquisition to further improve throughput in CT examina-
tions. FEATURES
• Wide range of slice thicknesses
This detector is provided with detector elements that
have high-power and uniform output characteristics, per-
mitting scanning with a minimum scan slice thickness of
0.5 mm. Image slice thicknesses of up to 10 mm can be
selected based on the objectives of the examination. • Advanced image reconstruction
This system employs the helical reconstruction technique
TCOT (True cone-beam tomography), which precisely
compensates for the cone angle based on the Feldkamp
method, thus minimizing artifacts related to the cone
angle and providing accurate, high-resolution isotropic
images over the entire imaging field. In addition, MUS-
COT (multislice cone-beam tomography) reconstruction,
which has received accolades in 4-row multislice CT, can
also be used. • High-quality images
The system achieves low-contrast detectability of 2 mm
at 0.3% and high-contrast resolution of 0.35 mm. Multislice helical CT can be performed using thin slices
in routine examinations so that high-precision 3D and
MPR images can be generated from the high-resolution
voxel data. In CT angiography of the brain, for example,
a 40-mm distance can be scanned in about 4 seconds
at a slice thickness of 0.5 mm. • High patient throughput
In combination with fast scanning, the high-power 60-kW
X-ray generator and 7.5-MHU X-ray tube permit data for
routine examinations, biopsy procedures, and 3D image
generation to be acquired in one scan. Images of various slice thicknesses can be generated. For example, it is possible to reconstruct 5-mm to ...
